originality.rationale: The nearest full scientific texts, Pham–Xue arXiv:2610.29664 and Fraser–Rakhmonov arXiv:2503.15072, respectively establish global spherical extension/recovery estimates and general finite-field projection/Plancherel bounds. The new claim instead fixes a nonzero ternary quadric, restricts an entire character plane to it, computes every eigenvalue and multiplicity for every plane orientation, and determines exactly all rank-maximizing planes with an exceptional q=3 tie. Neither inspected statement implies these exact quadratic-shell, all-orientation numbers without additional geometric fiber arithmetic. Indexed research records on paraboloid, Gabor quadratic shell, Hamming sphere, and binary quadrics concern other objects/measurement operators. Unindexed projective-quadric calculations remain a risk.
residual_risks: Exact projective-quadric intersection numbers are classical; their combination into a full Fourier-plane spectrum could have appeared in specialized historical finite-geometry literature without being indexed under harmonic analysis.
The Kang–Koh primary article and every potentially related classical finite-geometry reference were not exhaustively read; absence of a matching search hit does not establish absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The two-dimensional full character plane is a natural fixed-budget q² Fourier acquisition model for a nonzero ternary quadratic sphere. The theorem gives a complete exact singular spectrum for every possible plane, the maximum recoverable coefficient dimension, all optimizers, a q=3 exceptional tie and a sharp tradeoff between rank and stability. The negative-radius-sign isotropic planes achieve maximal rank with a single nonzero singular level, a substantive design property not implied by general extension bounds or raw finite-field quadratic counts alone.
